name: Salsa Macha

ingredients.name: neutral oil, such as canola or vegetable oil
dried puya chiles, stems removed, and halved lengthwise

instructions.primary_message: In a small saucepan, combine oil and smashed garlic. Cook over medium-low heat (the oil temperature should not exceed 275℉(135℃), until garlic is golden and fragrant, 8 to 12 minutes.

When garlic just turns golden, carefully add the chiles (they may sizzle slightly when adding), and cook until softened, about 45 seconds. Set a fine-mesh strainer over a medium heat-proof bowl, and pour the oil mixture through the strainer into the bowl. Transfer the strained solids to a blender. Blend the solids on medium speed, scraping down the sides of the blender jar as needed, until evenly chopped, about 1 minute.

Return the strained oil to the now-empty saucepan and heat over medium-high until oil registers 163°C. Add peanuts, almonds, pumpkin seeds, and sesame seeds and fry, stirring constantly, until peanuts and almonds turn light brown, about 2 minutes. Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh strainer set over the now-empty medium heat-proof bowl. Reserve the strained nuts and oil separately and let cool to room temperature, about 30 minutes.

Once the oil is cooled, add the fried nut mixture and reserved oil to the blender. Pulse until solids are broken down into small pieces (about the size of the sesame seeds), about 10 pulses. Season with salt to taste. Serve or transfer to an airtight container and refrigerate. Stir to recombine before using.

stand_ins: dried puya chiles, stems removed, and halved lengthwise

description: Spicy and smoky, this Mexican do-it-all condiment packs a plethora of flavors and textures. Spoon it over tacos or pizza, add it to eggs, or serve it alongside your favorite grilled meats.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 55 min.

Optional or for serving: 1 dried habanero chile, stem removed (optional)

Optional substitutions: dried puya chiles → guajillo chiles

Notes: Morita chiles can be substituted with chipotle as they're both smoked chiles made from jalapeños. Puya chiles can be substituted with guajillo chiles since they share a fruity flavor. Chiles de arbol can be substituted with dried Japones or Thai chiles which pack a similar punch of heat.
Since salt doesn’t dissolve in oil it will settle at the bottom. Make sure to stir well before each use.

Make-ahead and storage: Salsa macha can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.
author: Octavio Peña
